clue.text: Spots cause of disease — a nameless disorder

parts.note: a germ is a microbe that brings on illness

indicators.note: in disorder, the letters of the words are jumbled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A doctor explains that a rash comes from some unnamed ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' looks like part of the medical picture but signals that A NAMELESS is rearranged to MEASLES, placed after GERM.
explanation.definitionFit: The illness is known for its rash of red blotches, so spots stand for the whole disease.

clue.text: Proverbial road metal down under

parts.note: the proverb says the road to hell is paved with this; road metal is paving material and down under is the underworld, not Australia

explanation.definitionFit: The saying holds that hell's highway is surfaced with well-meant plans that came to nothing.

clue.text: Frees awkward knots

indicators.note: awkward suggests clumsy, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone untangles some tricky tied ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a square knot, used by sailors to shorten sail.

clue.text: Sailors taking wine on island mostly show restraint

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, so ABS are sailors
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, with its final letter dropped

parts.note: Iona is an island in the Scottish Hebrides

explanation.surface: Seamen drinking wine ashore on an island are surprisingly self-controlled.
explanation.walkthrough: Tent is an old word for a red wine from Spain; 'mostly' trims IONA to ION.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding back from doing something, such as drinking, is a form of self-denial.

clue.text: Someone is slipping into understatement

indicators.note: something slipping is out of place, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A person gradually lapses into speaking modestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Someone' splits into SOME and ONE; ONE becomes I, and 'slipping' rearranges SOME + I + IS.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhetorical term names the figure of speech that plays something down, like litotes.

clue.text: A student beau is unduly effusive

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate on a British learner driver's car
a beau is a boyfriend or lover

explanation.surface: A young suitor is far too gushing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all over someone is fawning on them with excessive attention.

clue.text: Less than a gallop, even for a horse

definitions.text: Less than a gallop, even for a horse

indicators.note: less than the whole run of words, so part of them is taken

explanation.surface: A horse moves at a slower pace than full speed.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'gallop, even'; the whole clue also describes an easy bounding gait slower than a gallop.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy long-striding run is the gait a horse uses when not galloping.

clue.text: Sustained by one's stout when it's drunk

indicators.note: a drunk thing is unsteady, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going on their stout once it has been drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical direction means notes held for their full length.

clue.text: Girl invested in semi valued at very little

indicators.note: something invested in a thing is put inside it

parts.note: semi means half
worth means having a value of
Penny is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman puts money into a semi-detached house of little value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' puts PENNY between HALF and WORTH. A halfpenny was an old British coin of minimal value.
explanation.definitionFit: A ha'p'orth is the amount a halfpenny would buy, so a tiny quantity.

clue.text: Too many people are on the sulphur drug

parts.note: over means on top of, so on
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
a pill is a tablet of medicine

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a crowd of people are taking a sulphur-based medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names surplus population moved out of a crowded city into new towns.

clue.text: Spaghetti as served in scholastic get-together

indicators.note: food served in a dish is placed within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: PTA is a Parent-Teacher Association, a school gathering
taken as written

explanation.surface: Noodles are dished up at a school social evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is one example of the Italian family of dough foods.

clue.text: Publish one's petition

parts.note: one is I, and with its apostrophe-s it gives I'S
to sue is to petition or appeal formally

explanation.surface: A writer asks to have their plea put into print.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring out a magazine or stamp is to release it to the public.

clue.text: Returned girl's husband

indicators.note: a returned item comes back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name, and with the possessive it is EVA'S

explanation.surface: A woman's spouse has come home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husband' looks like a noun for the girl's partner, but here it is the verb meaning to conserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband resources is to manage them thriftily and keep them from waste.

clue.text: Grouse flesh

definitions.meaning: to grouse is to complain or grumble

explanation.definitionFit: A gripe is a complaint in slang, and cattle meat is the butcher's red meat.

clue.text: If you put all your goods here, there's not much underneath

definitions.text: If you put all your goods here, there's not much underneath

parts.words: If you put all your goods here, there's not much underneath
parts.note: a shop's front display; also the idiom of a person who puts everything on show with no depth behind it

explanation.definitionFit: The glass display area of a store holds the goods put on view to passers-by.

clue.text: Flower generation stuck in road block on way back

indicators.note: one piece is lodged inside the other
travelling back means the letters are taken in reverse

parts.note: a sett is a stone paving block used for roads
an age is a generation or era

explanation.surface: A new generation is trapped at a roadblock on the journey home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on way back' turns SETT into TTES, and 'stuck in' puts AGE after its first T.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is the botanical genus of marigolds, a garden bloom.

clue.text: Nevertheless, going round the forest was recommended by Candide

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other
read as never-the-less, with never as nought, so the letter O is lost

parts.note: taken as written
the Forest of Arden is the setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: A forest walk is said to have been endorsed by Voltaire's hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nevertheless' is read as 'nought (O) less', leaving GING round ARDEN. Voltaire's Candide ends with 'we must cultivate our garden'.
explanation.definitionFit: Candide concludes that tending one's plot is the best course in life, so cultivating plants is his advice.

clue.text: Back her old application to move elsewhere

indicators.note: taken back means the word her runs in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
use means application, as in putting something to use

explanation.surface: Someone supports an elderly woman's request to relocate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a verb meaning support, but it reverses HER to REH.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone new lodging is to relocate them to a different home.

clue.text: Contracts for last of Minuteman missiles

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: arrows are projectiles shot from a bow

explanation.surface: Defence deals are signed for the final batch of Minuteman rockets.
explanation.walkthrough: Minuteman is an American intercontinental missile; 'Contracts' is a verb (gets smaller), not a noun for deals.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that tightens or becomes thinner is said to grow smaller in width.

clue.text: Hatchway covering for bunk

definitions.meaning: a small hatch with a lid in a ship's deck or side
to do a bunk is British slang for running off

explanation.definitionFit: A ship's lidded opening has this name, and to hurry away is to scurry off.

clue.text: Novelist's deep depression

definitions.meaning: a novella by Joseph Conrad bears this title
a severe tropical storm system of very low pressure

explanation.definitionFit: Conrad wrote a story with this title, and a weather depression of great intensity is a tropical cyclone.

clue.text: It gave old soldiers a roof over their heads

definitions.text: It gave old soldiers a roof over their heads

parts.words: It gave old soldiers a roof over their heads
parts.note: Roman legionaries locked shields above them in a tortoise formation, a literal roof against missiles

explanation.definitionFit: The Roman tortoise formation of overlapping shields protected troops from above.

clue.text: Fishes for a date

definitions.meaning: the ide is a freshwater fish, so several are this plural
in the Roman calendar, the 15th of March, May, July, October, the 13th otherwise

explanation.definitionFit: Ide is a carp-like river fish, and the Roman calendar marked a mid-month day by that name.

clue.text: Possibly a tinker's copper vessel

definitions.note: from the idiom not worth a tinker's ..., an oath of no value

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A travelling mender may own a copper pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not worth a tinker's cuss' is a British idiom for worthless; tinkers were itinerant pot-menders, so the copper vessel fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an oath, something worthless, as the thing a tinker might utter.

clue.text: A parent, perhaps, but not a blood donor

definitions.text: A parent, perhaps, but not a blood donor

parts.words: A parent, perhaps, but not a blood donor
parts.note: a spouse's mother or father is a relative by marriage, not by blood, so not someone who gave you their blood

explanation.definitionFit: A relation through marriage, such as a spouse's father, shares no blood ties with you.

clue.text: Poet's carol is different

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: made different, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer's Christmas song is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico Garcia Lorca was a Spanish poet and playwright.

clue.text: Goddess of the horse age

parts.note: H is slang for heroin, also called horse
an era is an age

explanation.surface: A deity rules over horses in an earlier age.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus's wife was queen of the Greek deities.

clue.text: Hooter envelopes one in clamour

indicators.note: to envelop is to wrap round, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: hooter is slang for the nose
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A car horn swallows someone in a din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' looks like a horn, fitting 'clamour', but it is British slang for the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A din or racket is a loud and unpleasant sound.

clue.text: This paper is undercutting the rest for a start

indicators.note: under cuts into a word, splitting it so the other sits inside

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the first part of undercutting

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A newspaper boasts that it sells more cheaply than its rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undercutting' splits into UNDER and 'cutting', which puts UNDER inside THE, followed by R. The Thunderer is the old nickname of The Times, where this clue was printed.
explanation.definitionFit: The London daily earned this nickname for its thunderous editorials in the 19th century.

clue.text: Novel ingredients for a wine of Scotland?

parts.note: fruit crushed to make wine
taken as written
Cape Wrath is the northwest tip of Scotland, so the place stands for it, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A recipe lists the fruit for a Scottish wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Cape Wrath is the headland at the far northwest of mainland Scotland; the question mark flags the loose use.
explanation.definitionFit: John Steinbeck's book about Dust Bowl migrants carries this title.
